input.brief: AI/ML systems engineer: makes LLM inference fast and cheap on GPUs, runs machine learning across NASA's 300+ Pandora sun-tracking spectrometers

direction.name: The split stage
direction.idea: Half the screen never moves. One side is a fixed photograph (or object, or product view) that stays in place for the whole visit; the other side is a calm scrolling column with everything you need to read. The fixed half keeps the feeling present while the reader gets on with the facts, like sitting in the room while reading the menu. As sections pass, the fixed image may quietly change to the one that matches.
direction.composition: Desktop: a two-column page, 50/50 or 45/55. One column is `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh` and holds a single photograph filling it edge to edge, or the object centred on a flat field. The other column scrolls and holds all content in a single narrow measure (max 46ch) with comfortable padding (48–72px): name and one-line description first, then sections separated by generous space, then contact and footer. Headings in the scrolling column are modest (32–44px). The column grounds differ: photograph on one side, flat paper colour on the other, meeting at a clean vertical edge. On a phone the fixed half becomes a 60svh image at the top that stays sticky behind the first section, then releases.
direction.typography: A text-first setting: a readable serif or a calm sans at 17–19px, with one display size for the name. Left-aligned throughout.
direction.colour: The paper colour of the reading column is chosen against the photograph: a tone taken from its shadows or its lightest area. One ink, optionally one accent ink for links and the action.
direction.imagery: One excellent portrait-orientation photograph for the fixed half, plus three or four more that crossfade in as their sections arrive. Small inline photographs in the reading column are optional and should be few.
direction.richness: A full-height photograph always in view, against a quiet, well-set column of text.
direction.pitfalls: The reading column must be genuinely well typeset, since it is half the page. Do not put cards or grids in it. Check that the fixed image crops well at short viewport heights. In blind tests the commonest complaint was monotony: several screens of the same split with only the text changing. Change what the reading half holds from section to section (a list, a large figure, a table, a full-colour panel, a drawing) and let at least one section break the split and run full width.

hero.name: Menu column, sticky photograph
hero.blueprint: The viewport is two panels of equal width with a 12px gap between them and 12px outer margins, both with a 20px radius. Right panel: one photograph of the place filling it edge to edge (object-fit: cover), set to position: sticky; top: 12px; height: calc(100svh - 24px), so it stays put while the left side scrolls. A solid bar in the paper colour, 56px tall, lies across the photograph's bottom edge inside the panel and carries opening hours on the left and the address on the right at 15px. Left panel: a filled paper-colour sheet set like a menu card, everything centred. Its top row holds the wordmark, about 300px wide, in the centre with one text link either side. Below, at 34% of the height, the headline in a light serif at clamp(40px, 3.6vw, 56px) on two lines in the accent ink, max 18ch per line. Under it one sentence at 17px, max 40ch, then the single action as a solid rectangle in the accent ink. The lower quarter of the sheet is empty before the first section begins.
hero.mobile: The photograph comes first as a rounded panel 56svh tall on 12px margins, sticky at the top so the paper sheet slides up over its lower part. The hours bar stays on the photograph's bottom edge. The sheet holds the wordmark centred at 46% of the width, the headline at 9vw on two lines, the sentence and a full-width action.
hero.headline: A warm 3-6 word line in a light serif, at most 34 characters, centred on two lines.

type.note: A slightly narrow neo-grotesk with closed apertures, used at regular weight from marquee size down to paragraphs. Suits agencies and digital studios that want large type without heaviness.

palette.name: Bottle green, gold
palette.note: Bottle green covers the page and warm gold sets all the type, with panels one step lighter than the ground. The button is solid gold with green text, and photographs are kept dark and warm so the pair is not disturbed.

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Narrow column, empty field
sections.blueprint: A single text column 300–340px wide, its left edge at 15% of the viewport width, starting 64px below the section top. It holds four or five short paragraphs at 15–16px with leading 1.5 and one blank line between them; the first paragraph is in medium weight and full ink, the rest in regular weight and the soft ink. No heading, no image, no button; one underlined text link may end the last paragraph. The remaining three-quarters of the 1440 screen is untouched ground, and the section is only as tall as the text plus 160px of padding below. The column's left edge must match a line used elsewhere on the page (the wordmark's left edge or a later column). Where the page has a large object or a fixed photograph, this column is the small text beside it. Holds 90–150 words comfortably.
sections.mobile: The column becomes 78% of the width, left-aligned at the 20px margin, so a strip of empty ground remains on the right as a deliberate margin. Text stays at 15–16px with the first paragraph in medium weight. Padding is 72px above and 96px below.

sections.name: Title torn at the seam
sections.blueprint: A wrapper about 95svh tall per project holds a sticky stage of 100svh, split at exactly 50vw into two portrait panes of 720×900px, `object-fit: cover`, square corners, no gap: two different pictures or loops of the same project (the whole and a detail, before and after). The project's title sits on the seam, centred on x 720 at the optical middle: capitals in a heavy face at clamp(96px, 11vw, 160px), leading 0.8, tracking -0.04em, at most two lines, in one light colour chosen per project. It is set twice inside the one heading element, the second copy `aria-hidden`, each copy clipped to its own half with `clip-path: inset(0 50% 0 0)` and `inset(0 0 0 50%)`. Directly under it, centred, the discipline and year at 16px and a text link with an arrow at 16px. While a project crosses the stage, the left pane and left half-title travel up and the right pane and right half-title travel down (panes ±20svh, title ±30svh, on a scroll-linked timeline), so the name tears at the seam and lines up exactly when the project is centred. The section's two-word heading sits at clamp(28px, 2.4vw, 36px) in the stage's top-left corner, 32px in. Four to eight projects; the stage releases after the last. Under reduced motion the halves stay aligned and the projects change by crossfade.
sections.mobile: Keep the split: two strips 195px wide running the full height of the screen with the same opposing travel. The title drops to 12.5vw on the seam, at most two lines, with the discipline line and the link under it at 16px; give the link a 44px hit area.

sections.name: Square plate, spare text
sections.blueprint: One flat field split 50/50, at least 88svh tall. Left half: a single square photograph filling the half's width minus 40px margins, vertically centred, square corners. A large simple shape may be laid over it to turn the photograph into the object it stands for: a ring 86% of its width with a 6px stroke and a small solid dot at the centre makes a record; a notch cut by clip-path makes a ticket stub. Right half, a flex column with space-between: at the top a row of three plain text tabs at 18px (editions, years, variants), the active one in full ink and the others at 40%; in the middle the title, two to four words at 32–40px bold, with a 34ch description 48px below; along the bottom two filled rectangular cells side by side, each half the column wide and 72px tall, acting as the two actions, one in ink and one a tone off the field.
sections.mobile: The square photograph comes first at full width with 16px margins. The tabs sit under it as one row at 17px. Then the title at 28px, the description, and the two action cells stacked, each full width and 60px tall.

sections.name: The printed menu sheet
sections.blueprint: The list is one tall sheet of paper. A filled paper-colour panel 640px wide sits centred, or offset to columns 7–12, on a contrasting flat ground or a full-bleed photograph, with square corners and its top and bottom edges cut into shallow scallops by `clip-path` or an SVG `mask`. Inside, 64px padding and a centred, symmetrical setting like a printed card: the venue or section name at 40–48px, a one-line note at 15px, then three or four groups 56px apart. Each group opens with its name at 22px, centred. Items follow at 17px with 16px between them: the dish or service at the left of a 420px measure, the price at the right with tabular figures, and a one-line description at 14px in the soft ink under the name. Alignment alone links name and price; there are no leaders. The sheet ends with the opening hours as two centred lines. Holds 12–24 items.
sections.mobile: The sheet spans the screen with 10px of ground showing at each side and 28px padding; the scalloped edges stay at top and bottom. The measure is the full inner width and prices stay right-aligned. Group names at 20px, items at 16px.

sections.name: Founder's letter
sections.blueprint: A letter in a centred column 520px wide with at least 160px of empty ground above and below. At the column's top-left, a round portrait 44px across. 28px below it, four or five short paragraphs at 16–17px with leading 1.55, each two to four lines and separated by one blank line, written in the first person. No heading. The sign-off is the writer's name at 22px in the text face's italic, with the role at 14px in the soft ink beneath it. One phrase in the letter may carry a flat marker-colour background. Variant for a page built as an object: the letter sits on a filled paper-colour sheet 640px wide with 60px padding on a contrasting ground, square corners, its bottom edge cut into small scallops with `clip-path`, and below a row of 5px round dots a tear-off strip 72px tall that carries the email address.
sections.mobile: The column takes the full width with 24px margins; text at 16px, portrait 40px. In the sheet variant the sheet spans edge to edge with 24px padding and keeps its shaped bottom edge; the tear-off strip stacks the email above a full-width button.

sections.name: Address in display rows
sections.blueprint: The contact block is a stack of five full-width rows, every one set at the same size, clamp(44px, 6vw, 88px), regular weight, left-aligned with a 20px inset and leading 1.0: the building or venue name, the street, the city with postcode, the opening hours as one compact line, the phone number. Each row is about 150px tall with the text sitting in its lower third; rows are told apart by alternating two flat tones of the section colour as full-width bands, or by 28px of space alone. A sixth row holds a one-word greeting at the same size followed, 24px to its right and centred on the x-height, by a solid round button 0.9em across with an arrow, which opens the email or booking link. Street and phone rows are links (map, call). No heading and no form. Optionally, one small round photograph sits at the right end of the first row.
sections.mobile: Rows at 9.6vw with 16px insets, about 84px tall; the hours break onto two rows (days, then times). The greeting row becomes a full-width band in the accent colour with the round arrow button at its right end, 56px across.

sections.name: Photograph half, menu half
sections.blueprint: A split footer one viewport tall. The left half is a single photograph filling columns 1–6 edge to edge, cropped hard by the left and bottom viewport edges: a close crop of the page's main subject, larger than it appeared anywhere above. The right half, on a flat field, is the site's menu set large: five or six section names stacked as links at about 2.6vw bold, 28px apart, starting at column 8 and 80px from the top. Rows are separated by space only; on hover a row's label shifts right by 12px and the others drop to the softer ink. Under the menu, 64px lower, two short blocks at 15px side by side: contact and social. The legal line runs along the very bottom of the right half at 12px. The wordmark sits small at the top of the right half, on the menu's left edge.
sections.mobile: The photograph leads at full width and 50svh, cropped tight. The menu follows on the flat field at 8vw per item with 20px between items, then contact and social stacked at 15px, then the legal line at 12px. The wordmark sits small above the menu.

references.name: Le Petit Bleu
references.idea: The cafe's teal-and-white stripes become the whole system: one teal ink on cream, everything boxed in thin double outlines like printed menu cards, beside a permanently visible photo of the room.
references.hero: Viewport split 50/50 with 12px gaps. Left: a cream panel with a thin pale-teal outline and rounded corners. Inside, a second outlined box is the nav bar: two-line hamburger left, teal brush-script logo about 300px wide centred, a caps order link right. Below, a two-line light serif headline at about 3.5vw, centred, in teal, then two centred stacks, each a bold caps label, a serif line and a solid teal button wrapped in a second thin outline. Right: a full-height rounded photo of a striped booth, with an outlined hours bar across its top, three slide dots bottom-left and a white address card bottom-right.
references.type: Self Modern, a light bookish serif, for headline and 15px body; Matter SQ bold caps for labels and buttons; Archive Mono Pro typewriter caps for menu rows; a brush-script logo. Section titles are tall condensed serif caps sized so four to seven letters fill the column.
references.colour: #fcfbf7 #13a7b2 #058599 #cfe5e7 #e9b81f — Cream paper and a single teal used for every word, rule, outline and button; no black anywhere. Yellow, floral reds and marble enter only through the interior photographs.
references.imagery: Bright, saturated interior and food photographs; the right-hand panel is a full-height slideshow with rounded corners. Small food shots sit in a horizontal strip, and a fine line drawing of the shopfront with one teal awning fills a card.
references.layout: The left half scrolls as a stack of outlined cream cards (full-width or two-up) with 12px gaps while the right half stays fixed. Card contents are centred. A sticky nav card rides over the stack. On mobile the photo becomes the hero card's background.

sections.description: A card containing only the section word in tall condensed serif caps, teal, sized so its four letters fill the column edge to edge. Below it, a stack of full-width outlined rows about 36px high, each with a category name in typewriter mono caps at left and a thin plus sign at right, separated by 6px gaps. Above the title: a ticker row of tiny caps and a strip of four small food photos with rounded corners.

The same giant condensed title treatment, then centred serif paragraphs in teal with underlined links in a narrow measure of about 280px. Further down, a landscape photo of the two proprietors with a centred two-line caption in tiny sans, followed by more centred paragraphs. All of it lives in the left half while the right photo panel has advanced to a shelf-wall image.

A header row with a tiny bold caps label at left and a script follow-us link with arrow at right, then three portrait images (about 3:5) with 12px rounded corners in a row, the third cropped by the column edge to imply a carousel. Directly below, the next giant section title begins and is cropped by the viewport.

steal: Print everything in one brand ink on cream, including body text, rules and buttons, and let photographs supply the other colours.
Wrap buttons and panels in a second thin outline offset by a few pixels to get a printed-ticket feel.
Keep a tall photo panel fixed on one half and scroll a stack of cards on the other, swapping the photo as sections change.

references.name: Flowjam
references.idea: A persistent frosted sidebar card holds the pitch and buttons while a soft-serif content column scrolls past it; beyond that there is no idea stronger than proof by logos and videos.
references.hero: Grainy off-white page. A tall rounded card about 26% of the viewport wide is pinned at the left and runs off the bottom; frosted over blurred pink and yellow flowers, it holds the logo, a two-line serif tagline, a short blurb and two pill buttons in hot pink and charcoal. The main column starts 32% from the left: a hot-pink pill badge, a three-line serif headline at 4.2vw, then a paragraph whose first sentence is grey and the rest black. A lone charcoal pill button floats far right at mid-height. Below: a heart icon with a proof line, then the top of a four-column logo grid with dotted borders.
references.type: Gelica throughout: a soft, slightly bulbous serif at regular weight, 60px headline with tight -0.05em tracking, 16 to 19px body, down to about 9px in the sidebar. One family for everything including buttons keeps the tone warm but flattens the difference between labels and prose.
references.colour: #f8f8f6 #e7e8e4 #1c0f1f #ff4fe0 #0c0c0c #7b3ff2 — Warm paper white with grain, near-black aubergine text and one hot-pink accent used for the badge and primary button; a purple heart appears once. The footer flips to black.
references.imagery: Rounded-corner video thumbnails of founders talking to camera and product UI clips, each with a small round play button bottom-left; monochrome client logos in a dotted-line grid; blurred floral blobs behind the frosted sidebar.
references.layout: A fixed 26% sidebar card at left for the whole scroll; content occupies one column to its right, split into two for video tiles and four for logos. Sections are separated by whitespace only. The footer is a rounded black panel that still leaves the sidebar in place.

sections.description: Four-column grid of client logos drawn with faint dotted cell borders, each cell roughly 240px wide and 115px tall with the logo centred in dark grey monochrome. Sixteen or more logos over four rows, no captions. Above it, a centred line with a purple heart glyph and a sentence whose first word is black and the rest grey serves as the heading.

Two-column grid of video cards. Each card has a header row with the client name in 14px serif and a one-line result in tiny grey beneath it at left, and a small outlined pill link at right; then a 16:9 thumbnail with about 10px radius and a round play button over its bottom-left corner. Cards are divided by hairlines rather than boxes, and some thumbnails are flat type frames instead of photos.

A rounded black panel inset from the page edges, sitting right of the sidebar. Its background is a short phrase repeated in dark-grey serif at about 5vw, rows offset so the words tile like wallpaper. Centred over it: a two-line white serif headline at about 2.5vw and a small stat line. The lower third holds the logo at left and four narrow columns of tiny text.

steal: Pin a narrow card with logo, one-line pitch and both actions beside the scrolling content, so the call to action never leaves the screen and no top nav is needed.
Set one sentence of a paragraph in grey and the rest in black to rank two claims without changing size or weight.
Tile a short phrase as dark-on-black wallpaper behind the footer headline.

references.name: bleibtgleich’26
references.idea: One thin vertical rule runs down the page and a tight bold grotesk sentence wraps around it, words stepping from one side of the line to the other.
references.hero: White page, black type. Content sits in a narrow band between 26% and 68% of the width. A 1px vertical rule drops from the top edge at 37% for two-thirds of the height. Left of it: a black blob avatar at the top, a tiny role caption at its foot. Right of it: a tiny location note at the top, the name in two lines of 90px medium grotesk at the bottom. The tagline continues below at the same size, flush to the band's left edge, running past the fold. The upper half is otherwise blank. The handle is split into two pale-grey words fixed in the bottom corners; a black menu pill sits top-right.
references.type: Akzidenz Grotesk Pro medium only, -0.05em tracking, line-height about 0.9. Two sizes: 90px (6.3vw) for every statement and 11-13px for captions and table rows, a 7:1 jump. Long words are hyphenated and stepped across lines on purpose.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #e4e4e4 #f2f2f2 — Black on white with no accent. Pale grey is used for the ghosted corner wordmark and a few small square tiles; tiny coloured rings inside those tiles are the only hue.
references.imagery: Almost none: a black blob avatar, a few 85px grey tiles each with a coloured ring, and a canvas dome of small tilted project thumbnails floating between two words.
references.layout: Everything hangs off one vertical axis at 37%: lines start either at the axis or one indent to its left, giving a stepped rag. Very wide white margins. Sections are separated by a full screen of white rather than rules or colour.

sections.description: A 90px sentence is typeset word by word around the vertical rule: one word ends just left of the rule, the next starts just right of it, and the following line is centred beneath both. Above the sentence a row of five 85px pale-grey squares, each with a small coloured ring at its centre, is spaced unevenly along one baseline, with a three-line 13px description under the second.

The heading first appears as one centred line near the bottom of an empty screen, then its two halves separate to the far left and far right edges at mid-height. In the gap a WebGL dome of fifteen or so small project thumbnails, mostly black and white, tilts in perspective like tiles on a sphere. Nothing else is on the screen.

The heading is broken into an ampersand alone in the left margin and two words stepped over three lines with a hyphen break and a growing indent. Below it a four-column table at 11px: year, site name, awarding body, award. Hairline rules sit under every row, columns align to the hero's band, and year groups are separated by a blank row.

The closing sentence is stepped over four lines with shifting indents, right of centre. To its left two tiny grey captions and an email address at 11px. Under it three 36px outlined circles with social initials, centred, then the handle at about 44px centred on the bottom edge with tiny legal text in the two corners.

steal: Draw one 1px vertical rule and typeset a large sentence around it, alternating words to either side so the line becomes the text's spine.
Split the logotype into two words, ghost them at about 10% grey, and fix one in each bottom corner of the viewport.
Leave the top half of the hero blank and start the name at 50% height so the headline runs off the fold and pulls the scroll.
references.media: No picture on the first screen, which is all type plus a small black mark. Pictures arrive later as a WebGL sphere of project thumbnails flanked by two words that slide apart on scroll, square tiles placed on separate grid cells with empty cells between them, hover thumbnails behind a text index, and one small image used as a glyph in a row of numerals; no video.
references.motion: A 2.5s progress counter runs although the page loaded in 1.5s, while a vertical line draws down with the role label at its tip. Lenis and 15 ScrollTriggers with nothing pinned: display lines rise by yPercent over 0.47s in-out at a 0.075s stagger, the globe's rotation is scrubbed across its 1178px block, the flanking words are pulled apart on a scrub, and underlines wipe in by background-size over 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.76,0,0.24,1).
